key_insight: Diffusion-activated epitaxy combines two metastable synthesis routes to expand the accessible synthesis window and stabilize novel crystal phases.
engineering_relevance: This approach could speed discovery of quantum materials by making previously inaccessible, metastable compounds experimentally reachable.
method: Combine diffusion and epitaxy in a single synthesis strategy.
Sweep a narrow synthesis space to search for stabilizable phases.
Characterize products with X-ray diffraction and scanning transmission electron microscopy.
evidence_signal: Within a narrow synthesis window, the authors stabilized four distinct phases, and three showed XRD/STEM signatures inconsistent with known experimental and computational crystal structures.
watch_item: The demonstrated phase stabilization was observed in a narrow investigated parameter space, so reproducibility and generality across broader material systems still need validation.
paper_title: Doubly Metastable Synthesis for Accelerated Quantum Materials Discovery
